race_context: The district: the 'Morgan MSD Martinsville School Board' seat belongs to the Metropolitan School District of Martinsville (MSD of Martinsville) in Morgan County, based in Martinsville {nces_msd}{msd_rfp_2026}. The district lists seven K-4 elementary schools, Bell Intermediate Academy (grades 5-6), John R. Wooden Middle School, Martinsville High School, Hammons Alternative School and preschool programs {msd_about}. Federal data list 3,998 students in ten schools in 2024-25 {nces_msd}. Dr. Eric Bowlen is superintendent; the board selected him effective July 1, 2022, after he served as a middle school principal and then Martinsville High School principal {msd_about}{msd_rfp_2026}.

The board has five members: Luke Jackson (president), Dan Conway (vice president), Matt Hankins (secretary), Jacque Deckard and Heather Staggs {msd_board}. State election results list five numbered districts with one seat each; Districts 1, 3 and 4 were on the ballot in 2020 and 2024, and Districts 2 and 5 in 2022 {enr_2020}{enr_2022}{enr_2024}. This guide did not find the district's own description of residence rules or of which voters may vote in each district race.

Seat on the 2026 ballot: District 2, which elects one member, matching the state list's 'vote for 1' {in_list}{enr_2022}. Dan Conway holds the seat: he won it in 2022 with 4,051 votes to 3,700 for incumbent Don Lipps {enr_2022}. Conway is running for re-election and is challenged by Jordan Scott Terrell {in_list}.

District 5, held by board president Luke Jackson since he won it unopposed in 2022, would also normally be up in 2026, but no District 5 race appears on the state list {enr_2022}{in_list}{msd_board}. This guide could not determine why.
Party labels: both candidates are listed as Republicans on the state list {in_list}. In 2022 the District 2 candidates ran without party labels {rt_20220907}{enr_2022}.

Elementary consolidation: the district plans to close Centerton Elementary, Green Township Elementary, Poston Road Elementary and Smith Fine Arts Academy at the end of the 2026-27 school year and open one new elementary school for 2027-28, according to a December 2025 district announcement published by the Martinsville Chamber of Commerce {chamber_20251210}. The district said all four buildings were built before the 1960s and that maintaining several aging buildings costs more than building and operating one new school; it described the project as tax-neutral, built under a 'Build-Operate-Transfer' model {chamber_20251210}{fox59_consolidation}. The announcement said the board was scheduled to approve the plans on December 10, 2025; this guide did not find a record of that vote {chamber_20251210}. Then-board president Heather Staggs said the board's responsibility is to 'plan not just for today's students, but for generations to come' {fox59_consolidation}.

Bond projects: in May 2026 the district sought proposals for a $12.5 million package of smaller projects funded by general obligation bonds, including a gym roof at John R. Wooden Middle School, HVAC and other upgrades at Poston Road Elementary, Martinsville High School auditorium and cafeteria work, playground and furniture upgrades at four elementary schools, demolition at Charles L. Smith Fine Arts Academy, and solar at Paragon Elementary and the high school {msd_rfp_2026}.

Budget and taxes: the 2027 budget hearing was set for October 8, 2026 and adoption for October 22, 2026 {msd_form3_2027}. The published notice lists a $61.3 million total budget estimate; for the debt service fund it lists a maximum of $12,531,898 to be raised, 42.27 percent above the current levy of $8,808,726, and an estimated $946,000 in property-tax cap credits {msd_form3_2027}. This guide found no public statement from the board on how the 2025 property-tax law (SEA 1) affects Martinsville's budget. Martinsville is not listed among districts with referendums on the November 2026 ballot {dlgf_ref}.

Teacher pay: in October 2025 the Indiana Department of Education notified the district that its state tuition support rose from fiscal 2024 to 2025 but that it did not meet the state's minimum spending requirement for full-time teacher salaries, spending $14,227,991.79 against a required floor of $14,630,676.84; the district was required to acknowledge the notice at a public meeting and post it online {msd_floor_2025}.
Board meeting minutes are posted on BoardDocs, which could not be read for this guide, so individual votes in 2025-26 are not described here {msd_board}.
Forums and questionnaires: this guide found no 2026 candidate forum, newspaper questionnaire or VOTE411 entry for this race.

candidates.summary: Incumbent and board vice president, first elected in 2022 {enr_2022}{msd_board}.
background: Won the District 2 seat in 2022, defeating incumbent Don Lipps {enr_2022}{rt_20221103}.
path_to_ballot: Listed as a Republican on the state list {in_list}.

items: As a 2022 candidate, named bullying as a challenge for the district: 'I've heard a lot of concerns from different folks about the bullying, about how we report it and then what are we doing to correct it,' and said he was meeting with a district to see how it handles and reports bullying {rt_20221103}.

In 2022 said the district should find out why families who live in the MSD send their children elsewhere, saying he had asked parents at other schools, 'What is your negative to Martinsville?', and that the district should address their concerns with 'more of an action plan' {rt_20221103}.
